name: The Corinthians at the Lord’s supper
charge: Eating and drinking unworthily; shaming them that have not
summary: When the Corinthians came together it was not for the better but for the worse: there were divisions among them, every one took his own supper before another, one was hungry and another drunken, and those who had nothing were shamed (1 Corinthians 11:17-22). Paul asked whether they had no houses to eat and drink in, and told them they despised the congregation of God. For that cause many among them were weak and sickly, and many slept; being judged, they were chastened of the Lord, that they should not be condemned with the world (1 Corinthians 11:30-32).
offenseFull: The supper was given for unification. The cup of blessing is the communion of the blood of Christ and the bread the communion of his body, and being many we are one bread and one body, all partakers of that one bread (1 Corinthians 10:16-17). The northern and southern kingdoms were divided and he brought us under one head; the table is where that is shown. So a man does not come into the assembly and eat all the food, drink all the drink, and get drunk with no moderation while a brother sits there with nothing. That is not the Lord’s supper, however often it is called that (1 Corinthians 11:17-22). Paul also told them there must be heresies among them, so that they which are approved may be made manifest (1 Corinthians 11:19); the breaking of bread is exactly where it shows, because a man can sit and break bread with a body whose faith he does not share.

Paul returned them to what he had received and delivered: the bread given in remembrance, and the cup as the new testament in his blood, and as often as they eat and drink they show the Lord’s death till he come (1 Corinthians 11:23-26). To eat and drink unworthily is to do it out of that mind, not discerning the Lord’s body, and it makes a man guilty of the body and blood of the Lord and brings damnation on himself (1 Corinthians 11:27-29). What a man sows is what he reaps: sowing to the flesh reaps corruption, sowing to the spirit reaps life everlasting (Galatians 6:7-8). And the assembling is not to be forsaken, as the manner of some is, but so much the more as the day is seen approaching (Hebrews 10:25).
judgmentFull: For this cause many were weak and sickly among them, and many slept (1 Corinthians 11:30). The teaching turns the verse into an inventory. Examine whether you actually have a charitable spirit, whether you are looking out for the people sitting around you or serving your own belly, and you will find how much of the body is sick and how much of it is still asleep to the understanding of Christ. When we say Israel is sick, this is what is meant. If we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged (1 Corinthians 11:31).

The sentence on that congregation was correction and not destruction. When we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world (1 Corinthians 11:32), and the instruction that follows is plain and domestic: when they come together to eat, tarry one for another, and let the man who is hungry eat at home, so that they do not come together to condemnation (1 Corinthians 11:33-34). The Lord chastens the son he loves and scourges every son he receives, and the chastening is neither to be despised nor fainted under, because it is proof of sonship (Hebrews 12:5-8; Proverbs 3:11-12).

taught.title: Proverbs 3: Trust in the Lord with All Thine Heart

lawsResolved.text: Give no offense to the church of God.
Partaking of Communion in remembrance of Christ and in celebration of the Lord's supper.
Acts of uncharitableness towards the poor are condemned.
God chastises and punishes only His sons who He loves, for if you receive not chastisement, then are you bastards and not sons.
Every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labor.

text.text: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?
For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.
Now in this that I declare unto you I praise you not, that ye come together not for the better, but for the worse.
For first of all, when ye come together in the church, I hear that there be divisions among you; and I partly believe it.
For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.
When ye come together therefore into one place, this is not to eat the Lord’s supper.
For in eating every one taketh before other his own supper: and one is hungry, and another is drunken.
What? have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise ye the church of God, and shame them that have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I praise you not.
For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.
For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, That the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread:
And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.
After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.
For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come.
Wherefore whosoever shall eat this bread, and drink this cup of the Lord, unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup.
For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body.
Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.
For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.
Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep.
For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.
But when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world.
Wherefore, my brethren, when ye come together to eat, tarry one for another.
And if any man hunger, let him eat at home; that ye come not together unto condemnation. And the rest will I set in order when I come.
And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:
For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?
But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of his correction:
For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.
